role.hint: This one is about the person’s job, skills or place in the organization, not the company and not their feelings.

company.hint: This one describes the company: its size, industry or tools.

pain.d: What frustrates them, in their words
pain.hint: A pain point is a problem they feel today. Look for frustration in their own voice.

goal.hint: A goal is the outcome they want, not the obstacle in the way.

criteria.d: What they need before they buy
criteria.hint: Decision criteria are conditions a product has to meet before they will consider it.

signals.d: What they have done with you
signals.hint: Behavior signals are actions recorded in your CRM, such as visits, downloads and attendance.

cards.why: A behavior signal. They are actively researching how to automate reporting.

cards.text: Visited the pricing page 3 times in 14 days
cards.why: A behavior signal. Repeat pricing visits suggest they are evaluating cost.
Firmographic context. Size and industry shape budget and buying process.

cards.text: Opened the API and integrations docs 4 times
cards.why: A behavior signal. They keep checking how the product connects to other systems.

cards.text: Business Intelligence Manager, 6 years of experience
cards.why: Title and experience define their role and seniority.
Skills show how they work day to day. They live in spreadsheets and queries.

cards.text: Reports to the VP of Operations
cards.why: Reporting line shows who influences their decisions.

cards.text: Company tech stack includes NetSuite and Shopify Plus
cards.why: Company context. The tools already in place decide what has to integrate.

cards.text: “I spend half my week pulling numbers into a spreadsheet.”
cards.why: A pain point in their own words, ready to reuse in messaging.

cards.text: “My tools don’t talk to each other, so I rebuild the same report by hand.”
cards.why: A second pain point, about disconnected systems.

cards.text: “I need to show leadership which campaigns actually drive revenue.”
cards.why: A goal. This is the outcome they are trying to reach.

cards.text: “If it doesn’t plug into NetSuite, I won’t even book a demo.”
cards.why: A decision criterion. It is a condition for even considering a product.

cards.text: “Price matters less than whether setup takes weeks or days.”
cards.why: A decision criterion. Speed of setup outweighs price for them.
Nothing here changes how you message or reach this person.

cards.text: Probably a Millennial who prefers Slack to email
cards.why: A generational stereotype. It is not backed by data and does not explain buying behavior.
Personal income rarely affects a professional software purchase.
